title: POWER fractional exponent: 715 counted live rows, none cleanly held out
status_plain: 715 rows were counted against live Excel and all 715 matched. Neither half of the corpus is cleanly held out from the algorithm the 715 describes: the 315 rows are the reverse-engineering ground truth that fix (a) -- the y<0 reciprocal staging -- was solved against, and the 400-row "fresh confirmation" sweep is where fix (b) -- exponent |y|==0.5 is the hardware sqrt -- was DISCOVERED and then also scored. The label must therefore read 715 counted rows, none cleanly held out; the 400-row sweep is where the second correction was found.

counts.source_sentence: With (a)+(b) the full algorithm reproduces live Excel **400/400** on a fresh sweep spanning both signs, negative-base roots, integer, subnormal, and error rows.

evidence_locality_note: The 400-row sweep and the 315-row ground truth are not in version control; the in-repo run directory `smart-fuzzer/runs/w108-power-phaseD/` holds only the pre-resolution 220-row bake-off, still headed `Status: open_puzzle`.
substrate: fractional path `exp(y*ln x)` on the x87 exp/ln with a double-rounded product; `y<0` computes the positive power, stores to binary64, then takes one x87 double-rounded reciprocal; `|y| == 0.5` is the correctly-rounded hardware sqrt

open_question: No held-out corpus exists for the shipped (a)+(b) algorithm.
reader_warning: Do not read 715/715 as a held-out result. Both halves of the corpus were targets of the repair they score. The `0.5 -> sqrt` and integer paths are CPU-independent; the general fractional path is not, and carries the same x87 microcode caveat as EXP and LN on roughly 1 input in 2000.
